note: Pinned upstream toolchain for the TNCA backend (compiler_overview.md sec 15, C0). Values verified against the upstream repository, not transcribed from memory; re-verify with tools/isa/verify_pin.py.

triton.rationale: The plan names 3.8.0 as the stable baseline candidate and says not to chase main. 3.8.0 is the newest tagged release and already carries the automatic warp-specialization paths sec 1.2 depends on.

llvm.note: Triton requires its own pinned LLVM revision, not an arbitrary release. As of 3.8.0 the pin moved out of cmake/llvm-hash.txt into cmake/llvm-info.json, which also carries per-platform sha256 sums for the prebuilt packages.

host_status.consequence: The MLIR half of the backend (tnca-opt, the tnca dialect) cannot be built or run on this host until the pinned LLVM is fetched. Triton itself publishes no macOS wheels. The bring-up path of sec 11.1 -- TNCA IR -> assembly -> tools/asm/tnca_asm.py -> RTL -- is pure Python and does run here, which is why it is built first.
